title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The MERge processing

abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond duration coherent radio transients, some of whose sources repeat, but the nature and active lifetimes of their engines remain uncertain. Strong lensing by galaxy clusters provides a physical lever on this lifetime problem: a short campaign can sample emission epochs of a repeating FRB separated by years, and distinct bursts in different lensed images, given a known relative lens delay, set a lower bound on its active lifetime, whereas delayed copies of a single burst only encode the lens delay. Based on the cluster-lens model of MACS J0717.5+3745, we quantify the accessible range of emission epochs for finite activity episodes, observing windows, and discovery selection. For a source-frame episode of duration \(100~{\rm yr}\) at \(z_s=2\) and a source-frame rate of \(0.1\,{\rm h}_{\rm src}^{-1}\), a five year campaign conditional on discovery yields a \(95\%\) gain threshold of \(m_{95}\simeq25.6\), corresponding to a source-frame span of \(L_{95}\simeq42.6~{\rm yr}\). At the population level, combining distinct burst associations with same burst echoes provides a way to test specified activity durations with a finite lens catalogue, e.g., activity durations differing by an order of magnitude can be distinguished with expected Bayes factor above $20$. More broadly, these lensed source frame epochs enable applications beyond activity-duration tests, e.g., linking burst activity to the evolution of the engine and its environment. Galaxy-cluster lensing therefore provides a promising future probe for accessing otherwise unobserved source history and for distinguishing between different activity duration models.
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures
title: Probing the Activity History of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts with Cluster Lensing

abstract: We present a spherical Schwarzschild orbit-superposition framework for constraining the dark matter density profiles and stellar orbital structures of the Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies. We model the line-of-sight velocity distribution with a Gaussian mixture whose parameters vary smoothly with projected radius through a mixture density network trained on unbinned stellar velocities. This approach reduces the effect of statistical fluctuations inherent in velocity moments on their kinematic constraints. Their covariance and smoothing-induced correlations are included, and the halo parameters are sampled with Markov Chain Monte Carlo. Mock tests for this model show that the density profiles and slopes near the half-light radius are generally recovered well, although the inferred velocity anisotropy shows some systematic deviations. Applying the model to Sculptor, Draco, and Ursa Minor, we find that the enclosed mass $M_h$ and logarithmic density slope $S_h$ at the projected half-light radius are less sensitive to the adopted two different priors than the asymptotic inner slope $γ$, consistent with earlier studies. We further compare the inferred slopes at the three-dimensional half-light radius $r_h$ and $0.5r_h$ for a given stellar mass with FIRE-2 $Λ$ cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) cosmological simulations including baryonic feedback. This comparison avoids introducing halo masses or virial radii that are not directly observable. The inferred slopes are broadly consistent with FIRE-2 $Λ$CDM predictions, although current uncertainties and the limited SIDM sample do not yet allow a robust distinction between dark matter models.
comment: 29 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AAS journals
title: Beyond the Inner Slope $γ$: A Schwarzschild-based Probe of the Core-Cusp Problem in the Milky Way Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies

abstract: Understanding the formation and evolution of dynamic fibrils (DFs) in active regions is essential for uncovering the physical processes operating in the highly structured and magnetized solar atmosphere. High-resolution chromospheric observations from the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) show DFs with periodic up-and-down motions. We carry out a statistical analysis of 176 DFs around a sunspot. The mean values of deceleration, maximum velocity, maximum length, and duration of the DFs are $120 \boldsymbol{\pm 43}~\mathrm{m~s^{-2}}$, $15.9 \boldsymbol{\pm 4.5}~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$, $1.13 \boldsymbol{\pm 0.48}~\mathrm{Mm}$, and $270 \boldsymbol{\pm 63}~\mathrm{s}$, respectively. Several pairs of parameters exhibit correlations, most notably a clear positive correlation between deceleration and maximum velocity. The consistency between the periodicities of DFs and running penumbral waves is first identified. We further find that DFs in regions with more vertical magnetic fields exhibit larger decelerations and shorter periods, whereas those in regions with more horizontal magnetic fields exhibit the opposite behavior. These results, together with the presence of running penumbral waves, support the interpretation that DFs are driven by slow magnetoacoustic waves. Furthermore, the multiwavelength signatures of DFs from the chromosphere to the corona imply a potential contribution to energy transport and heating in the solar atmosphere.
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures; accepted for publication in ApJ
title: High-resolution Observations of Physical Properties of Dynamic Fibrils Around a Sunspot

abstract: Strong gravitational lens modelling requires the lens light, lensed source light, and contaminants to be separated in each image before mass modelling codes can fit the system. Within Euclid this separation has so far been done by hand, which does not scale to the more than 15,000 candidates in the Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) catalogue of Data Release 1 (DR1). We present AstroVink-TREX , a neural network that performs this separation automatically and predicts three flux maps, in a standard format directly usable by mass-modelling pipelines. The network uses a hybrid architecture, pairing a vision transformer encoder reused from the lens detection network with a parallel convolutional branch. A custom loss function penalises both flux and structural error, while allowing independent weighting per component. From the network's predictions we also derive the modelling centre, fitting region, conjugate points, and binary maps, providing all the inputs that a modelling pipeline needs to run without manual setup. We evaluate the efficiency of the network on DR1 systems against existing fits and through expert validation. Across approximately 3000 inspected systems, taking 75% agreement between inspectors, just 39 lens models fail because of a segmentation error. Following this validation, the network provides the component separation and modelling setup for every system modelled in DR1. With automated segmentation, lens modelling is no longer limited by manual preprocessing and can now operate at the same scale as lens discovery.
title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). AstroVink-TREX: Automated strong gravitational lens segmentation as input for mass modelling pipelines

abstract: We derive new constraints on the interaction cross section between dark matter and neutrinos ($σ_{νχ}$) that improve upon existing limits. We adopt a mechanism where neutrinos emitted from core-collapse supernovae transfer their energy to the dark matter halo via elastic scattering, transitioning a centrally cusped profile to a flat-cored profile. We apply this mechanism to Low Surface Brightness Galaxies (LSBGs), which are characterized by their relatively large sizes, low stellar densities, and measurements of dark matter cores. We improve upon previous methods so that each dark matter particle is counted at most once, which weakens existing limits, e.g., from the Fornax dSph by a factor of $\sim 50$. Applying our new method to LSBGs, we derive an upper limit of $σ_{νχ}< 8.5 \times 10^{-25}\,\rm cm^2$ for a dark matter mass of $m_χ=1\,\rm GeV$ at a typical supernova neutrino energy of $E_ν=15\,\rm MeV$. This constraint is approximately three orders of magnitude stronger than the Fornax limit derived with the same method and slightly stronger than the bound from the dark matter diffused supernova neutrino background (DMDSNB).
comment: 12pages, 6figures
title: Improved Bounds on the Dark Matter-Neutrino Cross Section using LSBGs

abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.
comment: 7 pages, 9 figures, 1 movie; accepted for publication in A&A
title: Numerical experiments on sunspot penumbral flows

abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$α$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)
comment: 24 pages, 11 figures
title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis

abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $δN$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.
comment: 33 pages, 4 figures, 1 appendix
title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory

abstract: Context. Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of the multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution. Aims. We investigate five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster ωCentauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour-magnitude diagram. Seismic models are constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explore a binary-evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars. Methods. The evolution of the parent stars is computed with MESA. The collision is then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution is followed with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we construct seismic models reproducing the observed frequencies of the two radial modes. Results. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe stars (blue stragglers) based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main-sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.
comment: Accepted for the publication in A&A Letter, 4 pages, 5 figures plus 5 pages of the Appendix
title: Asteroseismology of blue straggler stars in $ω$ Centauri. Stellar collisions as a possible formation scenario

abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) variability provides a powerful probe of accretion processes and dust reprocessing in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), as it is less affected by extinction than optical flux. Using multi-epoch photometry from \textit{WISE} and NEOWISE spanning over a decade, we investigate the MIR variability of $\sim$4.5 million color-selected AGNs. Variability is quantified using maximum--minimum amplitudes ($ΔW1$), excess variance, reduced $χ^2$, and structure function (SF) analysis over timescales of 0.5--10 years. We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability ($ΔW1 > 0.5$ mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability ($A_{\rm var} > 0.5$ mag). A subset of these sources shows flare-like behavior, identifying them as candidate changing-look AGNs or tidal disruption events that warrant further spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up. The SF analysis shows radio-detected AGNs exhibit the highest variability amplitudes, followed by X-ray detected and the overall AGN sample. The variability amplitude is strongly anti-correlated with the Eddington ratio, indicating enhanced variability in lower accretion rate systems. A weak positive dependence on radio-loudness further suggests a contribution from non-thermal emission in radio sources. These results demonstrate that MIR variability provides a robust diagnostic of accretion physics and an efficient means of identifying extreme and rapidly evolving AGN phenomena. The full catalog of variable AGNs is made publicly available.
comment: 17 pages, accepted in ApJS. The full catalog table is made available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23682572)
title: WISE-VAULT: Decade-long Mid-Infrared Variability of WISE AGN

abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius $R_{\rm L}/a$, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over $10^{-5}\leq q\leq10^5$, the expression reduces the root mean square error from $1.97\times10^{-3}$ for Eggleton's formula to $5.95\times10^{-4}$, while its maximum relative error is $1.39\%$, compared with Eggleton's $0.83\%$. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of $0.331\%$. The formula is monotonic, recovers the $q^{\frac{1}{3}}$ scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within $0.036\%$ of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of $10^7$ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes $0.217$~s compared with $0.450$~s for Eggleton, a speed-up of $2.08$. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, Accepted for publication in ApJ
title: Symbolic Regression Fitting for Roche Lobe Radius

abstract: The Ariel mission will conduct a population-level survey of approximately 1000 exoplanet atmospheres across its nominal lifetime, requiring unprecedented consistency in the treatment of stellar contamination of transmission spectra. We present a systematic comparison of stellar spectral libraries and modelling approaches for computing facular and spot contamination spectra across the full Ariel wavelength range (0.5-7.8 microns) for six stellar spectral types spanning F3 to M2. Using a surface resolved forward model with approximately 200 randomly generated active region configurations per spectral type, we compute contamination spectra at Ariel Tier 3 resolution and compare three 1D spectral libraries against 3D MHD stellar atmosphere spectra as a physical ground truth. We find that library-dependent differences in the facular treatment introduce systematic biases exceeding the Ariel Tier 3 sensitivity threshold of approximately 20 ppm across most of the wavelength range, for most spectral types and activity levels considered. These biases align with the absorption bands of water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and methane, rendering them indistinguishable from genuine atmospheric signals at Ariel's precision. Our results demonstrate hat the choice of stellar spectral library, in particular the faculae treatment is a critical and currently underappreciated source of systematic error for Ariel atmospheric characterisation. The impact on atmospheric retrievals is quantified in a companion paper.
comment: submitted to 'RASTI: Ariel: mission, science & community engagement' special issue, 6 pages, 6 figures
title: Model Choice or Model Bias? How stellar spectral libraries and activity modelling choices influence Ariel spectra- I. Forward model

abstract: We present PyVesta, an automatic data reduction software for fiber fed echelle spectrographs. PyVesta is designed to be used with different instruments, both high resolution spectrographs such as HARPS or FEROS as well as inexpensive off-the-shelf spectrographs like the Shelyak eShel II. Special additions were implemented to improve the stability and resolution of inexpensive instruments especially. PyVesta provides tools for all extraction steps from raw CCD images to continuum normalized spectra, e.g., CCD image corrections, spectra extraction, wavelength calibration, and continuum normalization. Our software is based on the software package CERES and was ported to Python 3, revised, and supplemented.
comment: 22 pages, 16 figures, 1 table. To be published in Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific (PASP). Link to the paper describing the hardware: arXiv:2512.05601 [astro-ph.IM]
title: PyVesta: A new Versatile Echelle Spectra exTraction and Analysis pipeline

abstract: B supergiants are evolved massive stars with low surface gravities and lower effective temperatures, with substantial radiation-driven winds. Generally, they have been studied assuming 1D spherical symmetry. We present the first multi-D unified atmosphere and wind models for B supergiants, especially investigating the effects of approximate NLTE ionization and subsurface turbulence on the atmosphere and wind dynamics. We computed multi-D box-in-a-star RHD unified atmosphere and wind simulations of 2D/3D early B supergiant models using a hybrid opacity approach. We calculated line opacities from approximate NLTE populations, including line scattering. We calculated the flux-, energy-, and Planck-mean line opacities separately from our large line database using Sobolev escape probabilities, assuming two-level atoms. The models develop a highly turbulent atmosphere with time-averaged turbulent velocities of ~ 40 - 55 km/s at the photosphere in the 2D simulations, and ~ 25 km/s in 3D. In the cooler B1, B1.5 models, the wind acceleration is more gradual than in the hotter B0 model, leading to a significantly higher maximum wind speed in the B0 model. Further, the approximate NLTE formalism strongly alters the ionization stratification in the wind compared to LTE, modifying the line force. Mass-loss rates obtained in the models are of order 10^-6 - 3 x 10^-6 solar masses per year. Including turbulent pressure in hydrodynamically consistent NLTE CMF steady-state 1D simulations with comparable parameters can produce higher mass-loss rates and lower terminal wind velocities than in corresponding models without turbulent velocity, in overall qualitative agreement with our multi-D simulations. Our calculations suggest that in the lower surface-gravity B supergiants, in addition to modifying the photospheric density scale heights, turbulent pressure also influences global properties of the wind.
title: 2D and 3D unified RHD atmospheres and wind models of early B-supergiants including approximate NLTE effects

abstract: Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) is in a prime position to test Modified Gravity (MG) with Weak Lensing (WL) and Large Scale Structure (LSS). However, many nonlinear MG emulators in the literature enforce a $Λ$CDM background by design, missing where data suggest the most interesting deviations lie. We present an emulator for the 3D nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity, a Horndeski theory with a single additional MG parameter, $f_φ$, that modifies the background, growth, and lensing. Trained on \texttt{Hi-COLA} simulations with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), the emulator achieves $\lesssim 2\%$ accuracy for $k \leq 1.2\ h\,\text{Mpc}^{-1}$ at the fiducial cosmology relative to \texttt{Hi-COLA}, and $\lesssim 5\%$ relative to full N-body \texttt{EFT-RAMSES} simulations. Additionally, conservative scale cuts excluding angular bins affected by baryonic physics enable unbiased parameter estimation in LSST Year 1 weak lensing and galaxy clustering ($3\times2$pt) forecasts, even when validated against simulated data based on higher-resolution N-body simulations. This demonstrates that, within a simplified LSST Y1 setup and the adopted scale cuts, \texttt{Hi-COLA}-based emulation is sufficient to develop inference infrastructure with Stage IV precision for Horndeski gravity models previously unmodeled on nonlinear scales.
authors: for the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
comment: 37 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for submission to JCAP. Comments welcome
title: Cubic Galileon Gravity on Nonlinear Scales with \texttt{Hi-COLA} for LSST Year 1

abstract: The ongoing calibration of space-based instruments is essential to ensure accurate measurements of physical quantities such as photon flux. The goal is to obtain a unified photon-flux measurement of a single astronomical source using data obtained with multiple instruments. Calibration involves in-flight adjustments to address discrepancies arising from instrument-specific variations. Taking a statistical approach, we extend a previously proposed additive log-Normal hierarchical model with half-variance correction based on a multiplicative physical model for photon counts. The newly proposed Bayesian hierarchical model can leverage domain-specific priors to account for correlated passbands and integrate information across different instruments, sources, and passbands effectively. The model is fitted using Markov chain Monte Carlo and can provide uncertainty quantification for instrument- and source-specific parameter estimation. Moreover, we obtain valid inferences for other structural parameters of the physics model. We use data derived from Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray observatories to illustrate the proposed inference procedure.
title: Extended Bayesian Estimation for In-flight Calibration of Space-based Instruments

abstract: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. These observations probe the object's wavelength-dependent rotational variability, providing insight into the atmospheric processes underlying its infrared behaviour. Additional GTC/MEGARA optical spectra reveal that its H$α$ emission has declined markedly since earlier epochs, suggesting a reduced activity state during the JWST observations. We detect no emission from H$_3^+$ or absorption by hydronium in the NIRISS spectra. We use principal component analysis to identify two distinct modes of spectral variability: one dominated by FeH modulation near 1 $μ$m and another contributing broadband variability across the H and K bands. We find that no model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum. However, a blended model comprising an M-dwarf photosphere and a cooler blackbody component provides an improved fit to the mean spectrum, the broadband spectral energy distribution and the NIRISS broadband variability. By adding perturbations to PICASO model grids, we demonstrate that a combination of atmospheric heating and non-equilibrium chemistry can successfully mimic a blend of unperturbed photosphere and a blackbody, and that the presence of these effects may explain the unusual spectrum and variability of LSR J1835+3259.
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 15 pages, 14 figures
title: JWST/NIRISS-SOSS Spectroscopic Variability and Auroral Modelling of Warm Ultracool Dwarf LSR J1835+3259

abstract: Variability of massive stars indicates the presence of complex, multi-D physics near the surface. Recent advancements in multi-D radiation-hydrodynamical modelling of massive star atmospheres show strong turbulence triggered by the iron opacity bump. We analyze statistical properties of sub-surface turbulence in multi-D simulations of O-star atmospheres. Particularly, we study potential dependencies of turbulent properties on global stellar parameters. Using 2D O-star models, we studied several statistical properties of the turbulence that develops in these models. We compute autocorrelation functions of density and velocity to study typical eddy length scales. Moreover, we compute kinetic energy power spectra to analyze the energy distribution and compare this to known results from established turbulence theories. We find anisotropy of the turbulent eddies in velocity space. Moreover, this anisotropy increases with classical Eddington factor. This anisotropy disappears in density space where all models show nearly isotropic structures and no dependence on stellar parameters. The kinetic energy power spectra exhibit an inertial range with a cascade exponent that has an average value of -2.57. This exponent does not show any clear dependence on stellar parameters. Importantly, this energy cascade is significantly steeper than those in known turbulence theories such as Kolmogorov turbulence with exponent -5/3 and Burgers turbulence with exponent -2. This additional steepening can potentially be attributed to radiative damping which increases with increasing wavenumber. Sub-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars is anisotropic and radially dominated in velocity space and its energy cascade is steeper than both Kolmogorov turbulence and Burgers turbulence. Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
title: Properties of near-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars: Statistical signatures from multi-dimensional models of O-type stars

abstract: Theoretical predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and related projected statistics have been historically very expensive to evaluate, leading many analyses to rely on emulators to speed up slow numerical codes. We show in this paper that this need not be the case: improved numerical techniques can be leveraged to directly evaluate predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and projected statistics at speeds preferable for inference. We present bihalofit-JAX, an open-source, fully differentiable code for the nonlinear matter bispectrum based on the BiHalofit fitting formula, which includes numerous related projected statistics such as angular bispectra, skew spectra and aperture statistics. It computes $10000$ triangles of the matter bispectrum in $\sim1$--$2\ \rm{ms}$ per cosmology, one to three orders of magnitude faster than other implementations. It agrees numerically with the original BiHalofit code to better than $0.02\%$ on average over the cosmologies the formula was calibrated on, where the formula itself is accurate to $\sim20\%$ against simulations. It is also efficiently vectorised such that one can compute e.g. $500$ cosmologies in $\sim 2\ \rm{ms}$. This speed-up grows even more in the case of the third-order aperture statistics, which we compute in $\sim 6\ \rm{ms}$ for one cosmology, between $3\times10^3$ and $2.4\times10^4$ times faster than other publicly available codes. The pipeline is fully differentiable, and we demonstrate its performance in a simple inference problem, comparing the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) to gradient-free inference with the affine-invariant ensemble sampler (emcee).
comment: 20 pages, 12 figures, submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. bihalofit-JAX is available at https://github.com/AlexRoskill/bihalofit-jax
title: bihalofit-JAX: A Differentiable Code for the Nonlinear Matter Bispectrum and its Projected Statistics

abstract: Determining the Compton thick fraction ($f_{CT}$) within the population of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) provides insight into the evolution and growth of Supermassive Black Holes. Measuring $f_{CT}$ requires methods of modelling the AGN column density ($N_{\mathrm{H}}$), typically through spectral fitting which requires high source counts, or estimation methods such as the band ratio. We extend an $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ estimation method using the ratio of observed X-ray and MIR luminosity ($\log\left({L}_{2-10\mathrm{keV}} / {L}_{12\mathrm{μm}}\right)$), previously applied in the local universe ($z<0.1$), to a higher redshift. We used a sample of 47 bright AGN from the NuSTAR 80-month catalogue (NSS80) with a median redshift of $\langle z \rangle = 0.35$ as the high redshift comparison, and we applied X-ray spectral fitting to the NuSTAR sources with physically motivated AGN models to provide $N_\mathrm{H}$ constraints. The high-$z$ relationship was found to be consistent with the same model as the low-$z$ comparison, but with modestly different parameters which we determined to be due to a higher X-ray luminosity within the NSS80 sample. We applied the model to the full NSS80 catalogue to determine a statistical measure of the observed Compton thick fraction at $f_{CT}=4.9^{+2.0}_{-2.3}\%$ to $1σ$ uncertainty, consistent with other recent low-$z$ Swift/BAT measurements.
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS
title: Extending an X-ray & Mid-Infrared diagnostic for absorption in Active Galactic Nuclei to higher redshifts using NuSTAR and XMM-Newton

abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star.Methods. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.
comment: Submitted to A&A, 10 pages, 9 figures
title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023

abstract: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.
comment: 26 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series (IMAP first-results special issue)
title: A Multiscale Analysis of an Interplanetary Shock from IMAP, SOLAR-1, and the L1 Constellation to Earth

abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of $\sim5$ minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes -- slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma $β$ regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high $β$ regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies -- a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the $β= 1$ layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low $β$ plasma.
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures; Accepted for publication in MNRAS on 12 November, 2026
title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations

abstract: We revisit the production of fermionic dark matter $χ$ through the graviton portal, sourced by inflaton annihilation at the end of inflation. Because the production rate is helicity-suppressed, $\propto m_χ^2$, the dark fermion must be very heavy to account for the observed relic abundance, $m_χ\gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV, with the exact bound set by the reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH}$. Here we examine how interactions within the dark sector could modify this result. As a toy model, we consider dark QED, in which $χ$ couples to a light dark photon. We first show that, as a consequence of classical conformal invariance, bremsstrahlung of a dark photon does not lift the helicity suppression for light fermions. We then show that the trace anomaly of dark QED, which affects the coupling of the graviton to dark photons, can produce light dark fermions via a Dalitz process. This allows to extend the fermionic dark mass range possibly down to $m_χ\sim 10^7$~GeV, depending on $T_{\rm RH}$ and the dark QED coupling. We also determine under which conditions the hidden sector reaches thermal equilibrium and derive a lower bound on the temperature ratio at reheating $(T'/T)_{\rm RH}$ as function of the dark QED coupling and the reheating temperature.
comment: 18 pages, 3 figures
title: Gravitational production of dark QED by the trace anomaly

abstract: To evaluate the potential of detectors for next-generation space astrometry missions such as the HWO and Theia, an extensive analysis of the performance of the GIGAPYX-4600 46-megapixel CMOS detector from Pyxalis was conducted at IPAG. The 5456x8320-pixel detector, featuring a 4.4-micron pitch and back-side illumination, constitutes a matrix of 24x36 mm. It has a measured gain of 13.3 electrons per ADU in low-gain mode. The saturation level of the detector in low-gain-mode is estimated to be approximately 52 000 electrons. This sensor demonstrates linearity errors of 0.90%, pixel response non-uniformity of less than 1.3%, and readout and quantization noise of 12 electrons in low-gain mode. Dark current was measured at 35 electrons per second at 35{\textdegree}C and inter-pixel capacitance remained under 3%. We demonstrated that inter-pixel capacitance effects can be effectively mitigated using spatially varying kernel correction algorithms. Radiation tests confirmed its robustness against protons and heavy ions, and no latch-up was observed. These measurements agree with the manufacturer figures. These characterization results validate the GIGAPYX-4600 as a strong candidate for high-precision astrometry. Further improvements are currently being developed for space implementation.
comment: Journal of Astronomical Telescopes Instruments and Systems, In press
title: Characterization of the GIGAPYX-4600 CMOS visible image sensor in the context of high precision astrometry

abstract: The 21-cm hydrogen line brightness field is a potentially valuable source of information about astrophysical parameters during the cosmological Dark Ages and the Epoch of Reionization. However, it can also be a source of observational data for cosmologists seeking to constrain cosmological parameters. While much of the effort has been focused on constraining parameters using information across a broad frequency range, most often with the power spectrum of inhomogeneities, we investigate whether a single frequency channel, corresponding to a single redshift slice, can distinguish between cosmological models. We utilize topological data analysis to evaluate the possibility of such constraints. In particular, we use cubical complexes to perform persistent homology analysis of the 21-cm line brightness field. We generate 21-cm brightness fields of different cosmologies with the 21cmFAST package and then select snapshots at several redshifts corresponding to the Epoch of Reionization. Our goal is to find the redshift that is most suitable for highlighting the diversity between scenarios within a certain range of cosmological parameters. To compare persistent pictures built on simulations of the brightness field, we use Wasserstein distance, computed between any two persistent diagrams. We find that observations of the 21-cm field near $z=10$ have the potential to distinguish between cosmological models with different values of the normalized Hubble parameter $h_0$, the spectral index of scalar matter perturbations $n_s$, the matter density parameter $Ω_m$, and the matter fluctuation amplitude $σ_8$, even in the presence of instrumental thermal noise. We perform the PERMANOVA statistical test on the matrices of Wasserstein distances to confirm this hypothesis for all considered cosmological parameters.
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics
title: Distinguishing cosmologies with topological analysis of 21-cm hydrogen 2D brightness fields at Cosmic Dawn

abstract: The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distribution (SED). During a survey designed to find candidates to the aforementioned class independently of X-ray emissions, this object's optical spectrum was found to exhibit the typical emission features expected for a CBSS. The available photometric data show a quasi-sinusoidal modulation, with a period of 5.42 h, compatible with the orbital modulation of the system. Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B - V) ~ 0.7 mag.
comment: Accepted for publication on MNRAS as a Letter
title: A New Galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source Candidate

abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. We find a quantum efficiency of roughly 10 -- 40\% over this band, and fit these measurements to a quantum efficiency model constrained by these measurements and microscopy of the sensor layers. These measurements and the derived model informs this sensor's application within low-cost X-ray observatories, as well as motivates the development of commercial X-ray CMOS sensors without microlenses and deeper Si depletion layers.
comment: 32 pages, 11 figures, submitted to Journal of Astronomical Telescopes, Instruments, and Systems
title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass

abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Conventional mass-mapping techniques rely predominantly on gravitational lensing and often produce smooth mass distributions based on analytical profiles, potentially missing important internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve their internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy clusters to infer their mass distributions from optical observations. We subsequently applied this framework to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) programme. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Furthermore, the subhalo mass functions derived from the reconstructed maps exhibit power-law behaviour broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable and physically meaningful approach to mapping galaxy cluster mass distributions. This framework opens a new avenue for exploiting upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically investigate dark matter substructures across large cluster samples, complementing traditional gravitational lensing techniques. Moreover, the model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev--Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.
title: Precise Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Galaxy Cluster Mass Maps and Substructures from Optical Observations

abstract: The bi-Kappa distribution models anisotropic space-plasma populations with suprathermal power-law tails. Kinetic simulations represent such a population by computational particles, and a loader draws their velocities from the requested bi-Kappa distribution, which we call the target distribution. When $κ$ is close to 1/2, floating-point underflow can remove the largest draws, and a velocity bound changes the loaded distribution. Published Kappa loaders are usually verified by comparing histograms of the speed or of one velocity component with the analytic distribution. Such comparisons do not examine the direction of the velocity or whether the direction is independent of the speed. We build an anisotropic loader on an established Gamma-ratio construction and examine each of these problems. Near $κ=1/2$, evaluating the Gamma ratio on a logarithmic scale avoids the loss of draws to underflow in single and double precision down to $κ=0.5001$. When draws outside a bound on each velocity component are discarded and redrawn, a small rejected fraction can accompany a large change in the tail. At $κ=2$ and $θ_\parallel=2θ_\perp$, a bound at 20 times each component's thermal speed rejects a fraction $3.6\times10^{-4}$ of the draws and lowers the 99.9th-percentile speed by 11%. We test the loaded velocities through their direction and their normalized radius, the length of the velocity after each component is divided by $\sqrtκ$ times its thermal speed. The tests used nine values of $κ$ from 0.51 to 10, including $1/2<κ\le3/2$, where the second moments do not exist, with $θ_\parallel=2θ_\perp$ in double precision. At every $κ$, $χ^2$ tests find the normalized radius out to its 99.999th percentile, the direction, and their joint distribution consistent with the target distribution.
comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in APS Open Science (Data/Code). Code: https://github.com/KehengZhu/bi-kappa-distribution-sampling
title: Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision

abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.
comment: Accepted in ApJS
title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD

abstract: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.
comment: 28 pages, 8 figures
title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys

abstract: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.
comment: 63 pages, 1 table, 5 figures. Ready for submission to Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics (JCAP)
title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space

abstract: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. Setting up such a study takes many technical steps, and this work is increasingly done with coding agents, programs in which a language model writes code, runs it and checks the result. We present KELP v1.0, the Kinematic Engine for Lagrangian Particles, a tracker for unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix grids that is built to be operated by such agents. KELP computes two- and three-dimensional trajectories with established methods on triangular, quadrilateral and mixed meshes, with global FESOM2 and coastal FESOM-C meshes as examples, and on HEALPix, the equal-area grid on which kilometre-scale digital twins distribute their output. Documentation and short task instructions, called skills, tell an agent how to prepare releases and configurations, run calculations and process the trajectories. An agent prepared and ran all experiments of this paper with these skills, and most of the preparation was completed within hours. In a controlled evaluation, the skills raised the completeness of study files prepared by five language models from 75-93% to 88-100%. KELP reproduced the particle distributions of two other trackers on the same fields. Trajectories on HEALPix fields converged to those on the model mesh as the pixels were refined. After one year, the median distance between the two was 1.6 km at a pixel spacing of 25.5 km. HEALPix output can therefore be used for Lagrangian studies of ensemble statistics when the original mesh is not available. In a 63-year calculation with 7.92 million particles released in the Beaufort Gyre, transport from the gyre to Fram Strait took years to decades, and the run took 3 h 36 min on one 128-core node. A test tracked $10^{10}$ particles on a HEALPix mesh of 35.5 million wet surface nodes.
comment: 47 pages, 15 figures, 8 tables
title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids

abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $Λ$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address
comment: 4 pages, 4 figures
title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?

abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $Ω_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in $μ$ and $Σ$ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, $Σ<1$, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from $Λ$CDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.
comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables
title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
